fixes.x: A new fiber link between two switches will not come up. Both transceivers operate at the same speed, but one end has an -SR optic and the other an -LR optic. What is the problem?
fixes.e: SR optics are short-range multimode and LR optics are long-range single-mode; both ends of a fiber link must match in wavelength, fiber type, and standard, so an SR-to-LR pairing never establishes link.

fixes.e: Version control gives an auditable history of who changed what and the ability to revert to a known-good configuration. Interface alerting, device discovery, and session encryption come from monitoring and management tooling, not from the repository itself.

fixes.e: WPA3 is the newest Wi-Fi security standard, adding SAE key exchange to resist offline password attacks; WPA2 and TKIP are older wireless protections, and 802.1X handles port-based authentication rather than encryption.

o: A clean-agent gas system
A wet-pipe sprinkler system
A foam deluge system
A dry chemical powder system
fixes.e: Clean-agent gas systems suppress fire without the conductive water, foam, or corrosive powder residue that sprinkler, deluge, and dry chemical systems would leave on energized electronics.

o: Limiting internet exposure to only the systems that require it

fixes.e: RSTP, standardized as IEEE 802.1w, redesigned port roles and handshakes so the topology converges in seconds. 802.1D is the classic slow-converging spanning tree, while 802.1Q covers VLAN tagging and 802.1X covers port-based network authentication.
